simple.meaning: יָעַז (yâʻaz) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to be bold or obstinate.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Isaiah, beginning at Isaiah 33:19. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יָעַז (H3267) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: יָעַז (yâʻaz) / H3267 is traced through Isaiah 33:19 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H3267. yaaz [ יָעַז ] verb only Niph`al Participle as adjective (precise meaning dubious; Arabic is give a nod or sign , then command , whence Hebrew might have meaning nodding, making signs (not intelligibly speaking), so Hi — Che barbarous , De 'ungeberdig' — which context favours, or arrogant ; Thes proposes durus, saevus , and compare עזז ) — in phrase נוֺעָז עַם Isa 33:19 a barbarous (?) people , of foreign invader. יעזיהו יעזיאל, see below עזה . יַעְזִרִ see below עזר . p. 741.
